title: A diffusion-based 3D printing strategy to fabricate self-supporting networks
author: Betty Cai
materials: Paste G-code lines into G-code editing software, such as CAMotics.

Prepare crosslinking initiator solutions: e.g., 50 millimolar (mM) LAP or 2 millimolar (mM) Eosin Y disodium salt in PBS (Figure 4, center). For printing using alginate, prepare a solution of 1 Molarity (M) calcium chloride in PBS.
Sterilize supplies by autoclaving or by heavily coating with 70% ethanol, then allowing to dry completely in the TC hood, ensuring the inside of the Luer lock fittings is dry.

Gather required equipment, including print syringes, 27G × ½” blunt-tip needles, spatulas, Eppendorf tubes, and syringe holders for the 3D bioprinter (Figure 4, left). Figure 4. Sacrificial ink preparation for GUIDE-3DP. Left: Supplies needed for sacrificial ink preparation. Center: Crosslinking initiator solutions composed of LAP (50 mM; left) and Eosin Y disodium salt (2 mM; right). Right: Resuspended gelatin microparticle slurry (100 mg/mL).
If sterile printing is to be performed, filter the solutions through a 0.22 μm syringe filter.

Gather all printing equipment and materials, including the 3D bioprinter, syringes, nozzles, screwdrivers, DPBS, and UV lamp (if LAP is used as the crosslinking initiator) or white light lamp (if Eosin Y is used as the crosslinking initiator).

steps.title: Import reference model into Rhino
steps.instruction: Select reference images or 3D models from databases such as NIH3D, BioRender, or Vascular Model Repository and import the chosen file into Rhino3D (or equivalent modeling software).

steps.title: Create geometry in Rhino
steps.instruction: Draw the desired shapes or line segments using Rhino’s tools (e.g., Control Point Curve) to represent the intended vascular network.

steps.title: Divide print path into points
steps.instruction: Select the starting segment of the print path and use the “Divide” command to create points spaced at 0.5 mm intervals (or another set spacing).

steps.title: Export point coordinates
steps.instruction: Select all generated points, then choose File > Export Selected and save as type “Points (*.txt)”.

steps.title: Convert coordinates to G‑code
steps.instruction: Copy the XYZ coordinates from the .txt file into Excel, add G‑code syntax for each line (e.g., “G1 X(#) Y(#) Z(#) E(#)”), using extrusion values of 0.005–0.02 mm per step and a point spacing of 0.5 mm.

substeps.instruction: Create a column with the string “G1 X” & concatenate X value, “ Y” & Y value, “ Z” & Z value, “ E” & extrusion value.
Save the sheet as a .gcode text file.

steps.title: Add required G‑code headers
steps.instruction: At the top of the G‑code file prepend the following commands: “M83” (relative extrusion), “G92 X(start) Y(start) Z(start) E0” (set starting position), and a speed command such as “G1 F180” (print speed within 100–300 mm min⁻¹). Include any upward movement (e.g., “G1 F1200 X‑10 Y0 Z20”) at the end if desired.

steps.title: Generate G‑code for all segments
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 3–6 for every segment of the print path. To avoid extrusion between segments, re‑trace the previous segment with zero extrusion, or reverse segment direction using Excel’s Sort function. Add upward movement (e.g., 20 mm Z) at the final line if needed.

steps.title: Test G‑code visualization
steps.instruction: Load the assembled G‑code into a viewer or the printer software and run a test simulation to confirm the complete print path before actual printing.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M carbonate‑bicarbonate buffer
steps.instruction: For a 300 mL batch, dissolve 0.954 g sodium carbonate and 1.758 g sodium bicarbonate in deionized water on a stir plate until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Dissolve gelatin in buffer
steps.instruction: Add cold‑water fish (CWF) gelatin to reach 20 % w/v (e.g., 60 g gelatin for 300 mL buffer). Place the mixture in a glass bottle, seal, and either (a) shake at 200 rpm, 37 °C in a bacterial shaker, or (b) microwave in short bursts until warm, then stir on a hot plate at 37 °C until completely dissolved.

steps.title: Adjust pH to 10
steps.instruction: Measure the solution pH and adjust to 10 using 5 M NaOH, adding dropwise while stirring.

steps.title: Heat mixture to 70 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the gelatin solution to a beaker (e.g., 1 L beaker for 300 mL) and heat on a hot plate in a fume hood while stirring at 200 rpm until the temperature stabilizes at 70 °C.

steps.title: Add methacrylic anhydride (MAA)
steps.instruction: When the mixture is at 70 °C, add MAA dropwise at ~0.0833 mL per gram gelatin (5 mL MAA for the 300 mL batch). Perform the addition in the fume hood under stirring.

steps.title: React for 2 hours
steps.instruction: Maintain the reaction at 70 °C with stirring at 200 rpm for 02:00:00.

steps.title: Cover beaker to prevent evaporation
steps.instruction: Immediately after MAA addition, cover the beaker with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Purify GelMA
steps.instruction: Choose either ethanol precipitation or dialysis to remove unreacted MAA.

substeps.instruction: Ethanol precipitation: Fill a bucket with 3 × reaction‑volume ethanol in the fume hood. Slowly pour the reaction mixture into the ethanol while mixing with a spatula; GelMA will crash out as a gummy ball. Add fresh ethanol as needed until the solid can be lifted with the spatula. Collect the precipitate, spread on a tray, and dry for ≥24 h at room temperature.

Dialysis: Dilute the GelMA solution to 5 % w/v (1 : 4 with ultrapure water). Transfer to a 10 kDa MWCO dialysis membrane and dialyze against >2 L ultrapure water for 5 days at room temperature, changing water twice daily for the first 2 days and once daily for the remaining 3 days. After dialysis, sterile‑filter through a 0.22 µm membrane, freeze, and lyophilize.

steps.title: Load sacrificial ink into syringe
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL positive‑displacement pipette, transfer the prepared sacrificial ink into a printing syringe and attach a 27G × ½ in blunt‑tip needle.

steps.title: Add crosslinking initiator and beads
steps.instruction: Add the chosen initiator to the gelatin microparticle ink: 1–5 mM LAP or 0.025–0.1 mM Eosin Y disodium salt. Fluorescent beads may be added for visualization.

steps.title: Calculate gelatin microparticle concentration
steps.instruction: For the desired ink volume, target 100 mg mL⁻¹ gelatin microparticles (i.e., 10 % w/v). Weigh the appropriate amount of gelatin microparticles and resuspend in cold PBS or media.

steps.title: Seal and store ink plates
steps.instruction: Seal the ink‑containing plates with Parafilm and store at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Centrifuge plates to remove bubbles
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sealed plates at 4000 rpm, room temperature, for 5 minutes using a swinging‑bucket rotor.

steps.title: Prepare support bath in 6‑well plates
steps.instruction: Scoop 8 g of the support material into each well of a 6‑well plate (adjust volume if multiple constructs per well).

steps.title: Add fibrinogen for cell adhesion (optional)
steps.instruction: If cell seeding is planned, add 0.5–1 % w/v fibrinogen to the support bath to enhance adhesion.

steps.title: Add TEA and NVP if using Eosin Y
steps.instruction: When Eosin Y is the initiator, supplement the ink with 0.5 % w/v triethanolamine (TEA) and 0.2 % w/v N‑vinylpyrrolidone (NVP).

steps.title: Mix GelMA and AVC to make support bath
steps.instruction: Mix 40 % w/v GelMA stock with 4 % w/v Aristoflex AVC stock in a 1:1 volume ratio (or, for alginate, mix 4 % alginate with 4 % AVC 1:1). Stir thoroughly with a spatula until homogeneous; the bath will thicken as it becomes uniform.

steps.title: Autoclave stock solutions if sterile
steps.instruction: If sterile printing is required, autoclave GelMA and AVC stock solutions on a liquid cycle before mixing.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % AVC stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve AVC powder in PBS to 4 % w/v in an autoclavable glass bottle. Shake at 200 rpm, 37 °C or stir on a plate until fully dissolved. Wear mask and goggles while handling AVC powder.

steps.title: Prepare 40 % GelMA stock solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the required mass of CWF GelMA, dilute in PBS to obtain a 40 % w/v stock, and stir until fully dissolved (or follow the same procedure as for alginate if using alginate).

steps.title: Calculate support bath volumes for plate
steps.instruction: For a 6‑well plate, plan ~8 g of support bath per well; prepare extra volume for multiple constructs that will be crosslinked together.

steps.title: Store GelMA stock at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Keep the prepared GelMA stock solution refrigerated at 4 °C until needed.

steps.title: Determine GelMA concentration by drying
steps.instruction: Aliquot 50–200 mg of GelMA into 3–4 weigh boats, record the wet mass, dry the aliquots covered for ~24 h at room temperature, then weigh the dry mass. Calculate wt % using wt % = M_dry / (M_wet – M_dry) × 100 %.

steps.title: Redissolve dried GelMA and remove ethanol
steps.instruction: Place the dried GelMA in a beaker on a hot plate set to 85–90 °C, stir, and continue until residual ethanol (bp 37 °C) boils off for at least 01:00:00.

steps.title: Adjust GelMA concentration with water
steps.instruction: Mix the redissolved GelMA with ultrapure water in a 1:1 to 1:2 weight ratio to reach the desired final concentration.

steps.title: Dry precipitated GelMA before use
steps.instruction: Transfer the precipitated GelMA to a beaker, cover partially with plastic wrap, and let dry for ≥24 h in the fume hood before further processing.

steps.title: Set up calibration camera
steps.instruction: Secure a calibration camera onto the printer bed using laboratory tape or double‑sided tape so that both extruder needles can be moved into its field of view.

steps.title: Zero Tool 0 X/Y axes
steps.instruction: Move Tool 0 needle to the center of the camera view, focus by adjusting Z, then in the printer console enter: G92 X0, G92 Y0, G10 P0 X0, G10 P0 Y0.

steps.title: Set Tool 1 X/Y offsets
steps.instruction: Move Tool 1 to the camera center, issue M114 to read its X/Y displacement relative to Tool 0, then set the offsets with G10 P1 X(-#) and G10 P1 Y(-#) where # is the reported displacement.

steps.title: Calibrate Z axis for Tool 0
steps.instruction: Place a steel alignment block on the bed, lower Tool 0 until the needle just touches the block surface, then set Z zero with G92 Z0 and G10 P0 Z0.

steps.title: Calibrate Z offset for Tool 1
steps.instruction: Lower Tool 1 onto the same block, read its Z position with M114, and set the offset using G10 P1 Z(-#) where # is the reported Z coordinate.

steps.title: Reset absolute origin for both tools
steps.instruction: Move both extruders to the center of the bed near the bottom (within the support bath region if applicable) and enter G92 X0 Y0 Z0 to reset the absolute origin.

steps.title: Verify origin and adjust offsets
steps.instruction: Run M114 to confirm the origin reads (0,0,0). Move both tools to X0 Y0 with G1 X0 Y0 and check that Tool 1 aligns exactly; if not, correct offsets with G10 P0 or G10 P1 commands.

steps.title: Insert custom tool‑change G‑code
steps.instruction: Add a custom tool‑change G‑code block to the printer’s start/end scripts to safely raise and lower the extruder needles during printing.

steps.title: Warm support baths to room temperature
steps.instruction: Retrieve the prepared support baths from 4 °C storage and allow them to equilibrate to room temperature before printing.

steps.title: Load G‑code and mount syringe
steps.instruction: Load the finalized .gcode file into the 3D bioprinter software and mount the print syringe containing the sacrificial ink.

steps.title: Position nozzle and start printing
steps.instruction: Place the nozzle at the chosen start location within the support bath and execute the G‑code to print the designed network.

steps.title: Incubate printed construct for diffusion
steps.instruction: Leave the printed construct at room temperature for 5–15 minutes (or as required) to allow diffusion of the crosslinking initiator and formation of wall thickness.

steps.title: Photocrosslink construct
steps.instruction: If LAP is the initiator, expose the construct to UV light for 5 minutes; if Eosin Y is used, expose to white‑light for 10 minutes. Skip this step for alginate constructs.

steps.title: Remove and wash construct
steps.instruction: Gently lift the construct from the support bath, then wash it in DPBS (for GelMA) or HBSS (for alginate) to remove uncrosslinked material. Transfer to a fresh dish and rinse with gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Melt sacrificial ink at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the washed construct to fresh culture medium and incubate at 37 °C to melt the gelatin‑microparticle sacrificial ink.

steps.title: Open lumen ends and wash gelatin
steps.instruction: Cut open the closed ends of the printed lumen, flush out residual melted gelatin with fresh medium, and transfer the construct to a new dish.

steps.title: Adjust sacrificial ink pH to ~7
steps.instruction: After preparing the sacrificial ink, adjust its pH to approximately 7 using 1 M NaOH.

steps.title: Add endothelial cells to ink
steps.instruction: Suspend endothelial cells in the sacrificial ink to achieve a density of 1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Post‑print wash and short incubation
steps.instruction: After printing, diffusion, and crosslinking, extract the construct, wash with pre‑warmed culture medium, and incubate at 37 °C for 00:10:00 to allow cells to sediment onto the lumen surface.

steps.title: Flip construct and incubate second side
steps.instruction: Flip the construct and incubate for an additional 00:10:00 at 37 °C to promote cell attachment on the opposite lumen surface.

steps.title: Final wash and add thrombin if needed
steps.instruction: Perform a final wash with fresh culture medium. For fibrinogen‑containing constructs, add thrombin to the medium at 5 U mL⁻¹ and incubate for at least 02:00:00 to allow fibrin crosslinking.

steps.title: Alternative post‑print cell seeding
steps.instruction: Instead of pre‑mixing cells, inject a cell suspension (1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹) into the printed lumen, incubate 00:10:00, flip the construct, and incubate another 00:10:00 for cell attachment on the opposite side.

steps.title: Liquefy GelMA before mixing support bath
steps.instruction: Allow the GelMA solution to reach room temperature and liquefy; optionally heat briefly on a hot plate or microwave to accelerate liquefaction before mixing with support‑bath components.
